quizzes.title: SQL Basics Checkpoint
quizzes.description: Covers: Databases & SQL Basics, SELECT, WHERE & ORDER BY, INSERT, UPDATE & DELETE.

questions.prompt: Which SQL command reads data from a table?
questions.explanation: SELECT reads data. INSERT adds rows and UPDATE changes them.

questions.prompt: Which names does this query return (in this order)?
questions.explanation: Hira (60), Omar (80) and Sara (80) have more than 55 points. ORDER BY name sorts them alphabetically.
questions.code:
-- scores (name, team, points)
-- Ali  | A | 50
-- Sara | B | 80
-- Omar | A | 80
-- Hira | B | 60
SELECT name FROM scores WHERE points > 55 ORDER BY name;

questions.explanation: Two rows (Ali and Omar) belong to team A.
questions.code:
-- scores (name, team, points)
-- Ali  | A | 50
-- Sara | B | 80
-- Omar | A | 80
-- Hira | B | 60
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM scores WHERE team = 'A';

questions.prompt: What happens if you run UPDATE without a WHERE clause?
options: Only the first row is updated
Every row in the table is updated
questions.explanation: Without WHERE the change applies to all rows. Always check the WHERE first.

questions.prompt: Which names does this query return?
questions.explanation: LIKE '%a' matches names that end with a: Hira and Sara.
questions.code:
-- scores (name, team, points)
-- Ali  | A | 50
-- Sara | B | 80
-- Omar | A | 80
-- Hira | B | 60
SELECT name FROM scores WHERE name LIKE '%a' ORDER BY name;

questions.prompt: Complete the keyword that filters the rows.
questions.code:
-- scores (name, team, points)
-- Ali  | A | 50
-- Sara | B | 80
-- Omar | A | 80
-- Hira | B | 60
SELECT name FROM scores ____ points = 50;
questions.explanation: WHERE keeps only the rows that match the condition.

quizzes.title: Combining Data Checkpoint
quizzes.description: Covers: Aggregates & GROUP BY, Joins, Subqueries.

questions.explanation: GROUP BY makes one row per team: A = 50 + 80 = 130 and B = 80 + 60 = 140.
questions.code:
-- scores (name, team, points)
-- Ali  | A | 50
-- Sara | B | 80
-- Omar | A | 80
-- Hira | B | 60
SELECT team, SUM(points) FROM scores GROUP BY team ORDER BY team;

-- scores (name, team, points)
-- Ali  | A | 50
-- Sara | B | 80
-- Omar | A | 80
-- Hira | B | 60
SELECT AVG(points) FROM scores;

questions.explanation: HAVING filters groups after they are formed. Team A totals 130 and team B totals 140, so only B passes.
questions.code:
-- scores (name, team, points)
-- Ali  | A | 50
-- Sara | B | 80
-- Omar | A | 80
-- Hira | B | 60
SELECT team FROM scores GROUP BY team HAVING SUM(points) > 135;

questions.prompt: Which join keeps all rows from the left table even when there is no match?
questions.explanation: LEFT JOIN keeps every left row and fills NULL for missing matches. INNER JOIN drops rows without a match.
The join matches each book to its author. Ali has two books and Sara has one.
questions.code:
-- authors (id, name): 1 Ali, 2 Sara
-- books (author_id, title): 1 SQL, 1 Web, 2 Java
SELECT a.name, COUNT(b.title)
FROM authors a
JOIN books b ON b.author_id = a.id
GROUP BY a.name
ORDER BY a.name;

questions.prompt: Complete the aggregate function so the query finds the top scorers.
questions.code:
-- scores (name, team, points)
-- Ali  | A | 50
-- Sara | B | 80
-- Omar | A | 80
-- Hira | B | 60
SELECT name FROM scores
WHERE points = (SELECT ____(points) FROM scores)
ORDER BY name;
questions.explanation: The subquery returns the highest points (80), and the outer query returns everyone with that score.

quizzes.title: Database Design Checkpoint
quizzes.description: Covers: Keys, Constraints & Design, Indexes & Views.

questions.prompt: What does a primary key guarantee?
options: Each row has a unique, non-NULL identifier
The column is always a number
The values can repeat but are indexed
The column is the first column
questions.explanation: A primary key identifies one row and can neither repeat nor be NULL.

options: A second primary key in the same table
A column that points to the primary key of another table
A key that opens the database
questions.explanation: Foreign keys link tables and keep the relationship valid.

questions.prompt: Which constraint stops two users from registering the same email?
questions.explanation: UNIQUE rejects duplicate values in a column.

questions.prompt: How do you model a many-to-many relationship, like students and courses?
options: By repeating course names in the students table
With one column of comma-separated ids
It cannot be modelled in SQL
With a junction table holding both foreign keys
questions.explanation: A junction table (like enrollments) has one row for each student and course pair.

questions.prompt: What is the main trade-off of adding an index?
options: Faster reads, but slower writes and extra space
questions.explanation: The database must update the index on every INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE.

questions.prompt: Complete the name of the view to read from.
questions.code:
-- scores (name, team, points)
-- Ali  | A | 50
-- Sara | B | 80
-- Omar | A | 80
-- Hira | B | 60
CREATE VIEW high AS SELECT name FROM scores WHERE points >= 80;
SELECT name FROM ____ ORDER BY name;
questions.explanation: A view is used like a table: you select from it by name.
